title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 49 (Calls on Shares of Same Class to Be Made on Uniform Basis)

content.overview: Section 49 provides that where any calls for further share capital are made on the shares of a class, such calls shall be made on a uniform basis on all shares falling under that class. The Explanation provides that, for the purposes of this section, shares of the same nominal value on which different amounts have been paid-up shall not be deemed to fall under the same class.
content.glance: Calls for further capital on a class must be uniform on all shares of that class; shares of same nominal value with different paid-up amounts are not the same class.
content.study: Where any calls for further share capital are made on the shares of a class, such calls shall be made on a uniform basis on all shares falling under that class (s. 49). Explanation: shares of the same nominal value on which different amounts have been paid-up shall not be deemed to fall under the same class. Current-law framing: identify the class (using the Explanation); test whether the call is uniform across that class.

sections.heading: Uniform calls
sections.body: Calls for further share capital on shares of a class must be made on a uniform basis on all shares falling under that class.

sections.heading: Explanation — class definition
sections.body: Shares of the same nominal value on which different amounts have been paid-up shall not be deemed to fall under the same class for the purposes of this section.

provisions.title: Calls on shares of same class to be made on uniform basis

examples.title: Uniform call
examples.body: The company calls ₹10 per share on all partly paid equity shares of the same class (same paid-up amount). Section 49 is complied with.

examples.title: Different paid-up amounts
examples.body: Some ₹10 shares have ₹5 paid-up and others ₹8 paid-up. Under the Explanation they are not the same class; calls need not be identical across those groups.

hypotheticals.question: Can the company call different amounts on different shares of the same class?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 49 requires uniform calls on all shares falling under that class. Shares with different paid-up amounts are not the same class under the Explanation.

distinctions.title: Uniform calls (s. 49) vs acceptance of unpaid share capital (s. 50)
distinctions.left: How calls must be structured within a class
distinctions.right: Company’s power to accept unpaid capital not yet called

misconceptions.trap: The company may call only selected holders within a class for convenience.
misconceptions.correction: Section 49 mandates uniform calls on all shares of that class.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 49 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the class (apply the Explanation). II. Identify the call. III. Test uniformity across the class. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Class; paid-up amounts; call terms; uniformity or discrimination; precise relief.

examTips: Apply the Explanation: different paid-up amounts = not same class.
